The base changes the answer a lot: for all reporting agencies in FY2025, it is **52.2%** out of appeals decided on the merits (affirmed + reversed) and **32.5%** out of all processed appeals (including those closed for other reasons, e.g. withdrawn).
```{ojs}
- Across agencies, counts are added first and then divided, so large agencies weigh more (no average of agency rates).
- The FY2010 peak comes from DHS: 4,032 appeals reversed fully or partly, against about 1,100 in FY2009 and FY2011.

The top of the page gives both rates, whichever base the charts use.

**For the client to decide:** which base the charts should use by default, and whether "partly reversed" counts as a reversal.`,
  md`- **Growth** is the change from the year before, counting only agencies (or components) that report in both years, so agencies that start reporting do not count as growth. FY2025: backlog **+27.3%**, requests received **+13.7%** (117 agencies in both years; with all agencies, +27.2% and +13.7%).
- **Backlog is a stock, requests received are a flow**: compare their growth, not their sizes. "Backlog ÷ received" puts the backlog next to the year's intake: 0.23 in FY2008, 0.20 in FY2025.

**For the client to decide:** growth over the same agencies, or over all reporting agencies? Backlog as first reported or as revised?`,
  md`- **Any measure** from 31 of the 32 data types (214 measures). Not here: 06 (the laws behind Exemption 3, shown in Step 3), the reason texts of 03 and 11 (their totals are included) and the receipt dates. Names follow the annual report's fields.
- **Counts and dollar amounts** are added up for the government total. **Medians, averages, day counts and percentages** are not: pick an agency, or compare agencies in the table.
- **Right chart**: how many agencies (or components) report a value each year, to show where the data is thin before comparing.
- **Agency totals and component numbers** come from foia.gov's API (the team repository's component table). Where an agency reported the same component twice in one table, the two entries are added up, as foia.gov does.

**For the client to decide:** which measures to feature.`]
```

```{ojs}
//| output: false
// ---------- About the data: what the numbers are, the words, and the limits ----------
function about() {
  const revised = Q3.filter(d => d.level === "agency" && d.restated).length
  return html`<div class="about">${md`
### What this is

Every federal agency files a FOIA annual report. This dashboard brings the reports on foia.gov for ${SPAN} together, for the ${agencyNames.length} agencies that reported in any of these years, and their components. Agencies report these numbers themselves, and they are shown here as reported.

The numbers say what agencies did, not why. Response times and grant rates are shaped by request volume, complexity, staffing and the kind of records requested, so a difference between two agencies is a place to start asking questions, not a verdict.

### How agencies are shown

- **Agency total and component.** An agency's total already includes its components. A component is never added on top of its agency, and the government total adds up agency rows only. The top of each page says which one you are looking at.
- **Largest agencies first.** The agency list starts with the 10 that received the most requests in FY${FY_LAST} (${pct(TOP_SHARE)} of all requests). This only shortens the list. Agencies are not ranked by denial rate or given scores.

### What the words mean

- **Perfected request**: reasonably described and made under the agency's FOIA rules. Days are counted from this point.
- **Days**: working days, unless a table says otherwise. Decisions on expedited processing are counted in calendar days.
- **Time limit**: 20 working days for a request or an appeal, with up to 10 more in "unusual circumstances".
- **Simple, complex, expedited**: processing tracks. Every agency must have an expedited track. Other requests are reported as simple or complex, whichever best fits the agency's own tracks, so the labels are not identical across agencies.
- **Pending**: still open at the end of the fiscal year.
- **Backlog**: pending past the time limit at the end of the fiscal year. It is a year-end count, so years cannot be added up.
- **Full grant**: all the records asked for were released. **Partial grant**: some, but not all. **Full denial**: withheld entirely under exemptions.
- **Exemption**: one of nine legal reasons to withhold information (Exemption 7 has six parts). Counts are times applied, and one request can use several.
- **Appeal**: a request that the agency review its first decision. **Decided on the merits** means affirmed, partly reversed or fully reversed; the rest were closed for other reasons, such as being withdrawn.

### Blank, N/A, 0 and <1

- **Blank**: the component is not in that table, or the table was not in the report that year. Shown as missing.
- **N/A**: does not apply, or nothing to calculate. Shown as missing.
- **0**: for counts, the agency reported zero. In day columns and the "ten oldest" tables, a 0 usually means there were none of that kind, not zero days.
- **<1**: less than one day.

### Known limits

- **Who reports changes.** ${d3.min(PER_YEAR.values())} to ${d3.max(PER_YEAR.values())} agencies report in a given year, and only ${N_COHORT} report in all ${N_YEARS} years. On the government total, "Agencies added up in the total" can keep the same ${N_COHORT} every year.
- **Numbers get revised.** In ${revised} agency-years the next report gives a different backlog for the same year. The Staff & cost step shows both versions.
- **Reported totals do not always match.** In FY2025, Agriculture, Commerce, Labor and Veterans Affairs report an outcomes "Total" that does not match their categories, so shares use the categories added up. Components add up to the agency total in all but 20 of the 482 agency-years with components; Explore shows the difference when there is one.
- **Working days.** This rule comes from recent editions of the Justice Department's handbook; editions before 2022 have not been checked.
- **Cost** is not adjusted for inflation.
- **Laws behind Exemption 3** are grouped from many spellings. Names are titles from the U.S. Code, and the agencies' own words are in the Tables tab. Their counts do not add up exactly to the Exemption 3 count, which comes from a different table.
- **Not included yet**: the written "other" reasons and receipt dates.

### Sources

Annual reports from foia.gov (built ${D.built}), the Department of Justice Handbook for Agency Annual Freedom of Information Act Reports (updated September 30, 2025), and the U.S. Code as published by Cornell's Legal Information Institute (law titles and links). Each step's last tab explains how its comparison is made.

Student prototype for MuckRock (BU Spark! DS 701). Not an official MuckRock product.
`}<img class="about-logo" src="assets/muckrock-logo.svg" alt="MuckRock"></div>`
}
```

```{ojs}
viewof qi = {
  const q0 = +URLQ.get("q")
  const btn = (id, no, short) => html`<button type="button" class="qbtn" data-id="${id}"><span class="qno">${no}</span><span>${short}</span></button>`
  const home = btn(0, "•", "Overview")
  const steps = STORY.map(id => btn(id, stepOf(id), QUESTIONS[id - 1].short))
  const more = [btn(7, "+", "Explore all data"), btn(8, "i", "About the data")]
  const items = [home, ...steps, ...more]
  const wrap = html`<div class="qpick">${home}<div class="qpick-title">Step by step</div>${steps}<div class="qpick-title">Or</div>${more}</div>`
  wrap.value = q0 >= 1 && q0 <= 8 ? q0 : 0
  const mark = () => { for (const x of items) x.classList.toggle("on", +x.dataset.id === wrap.value) }
  mark()
  for (const b of items) b.onclick = () => {
    const id = +b.dataset.id
    wrap.value = id
    mark()
    wrap.dispatchEvent(new Event("input", {bubbles: true}))
  }
  return wrap
}
```

```{ojs}
// always shown, so it is clear that components can be picked; greyed out until an agency with components is chosen
viewof comp = {
  // the list is rebuilt when the agency or the years change; keep the chosen component if it is still there
  const valid = v => compChoices.some(c => c.key === v)
  const u = URLQ.get("agency") === agency ? URLQ.get("comp") : null
  if (valid(u)) window.__memo = Object.assign(window.__memo || {}, {[`comp|${agency}`]: u})
  const keep = recall(`comp|${agency}`, valid, ALL)
  URLQ.delete("comp")  // the address only sets the first view
  if (agency === TOTAL || compChoices.length === 0)
    return groupedSelect({label: "Component", disabled: true, groups: [[null, [ALL]]], value: ALL,
      format: () => agency === TOTAL ? "Pick an agency first" : "No separate components in these years"})
  // agencies with many components: the 5 largest first (most requests in the last year chosen), so small offices do not bury them
  const recv = new Map(ROWS.filter(r => r.level === "component" && r.Agency === agency && r.FY === hi).map(r => [r.Key, V[F.received][r.i] ?? 0]))
  const big = compChoices.length > 6 ? compChoices.slice().sort((a, b) => (recv.get(b.key) ?? 0) - (recv.get(a.key) ?? 0)).slice(0, 5).filter(c => recv.get(c.key) > 0).map(c => c.key) : []
  const rest = compChoices.map(c => c.key).filter(k => !big.includes(k))
  return memo(`comp|${agency}`, groupedSelect({label: "Component", value: keep, format: c => c === ALL ? "All components (agency total)" : compName(c),
    groups: [[null, [ALL]], [`Largest 5 (FY${hi})`, compChoices.map(c => c.key).filter(k => big.includes(k))], [big.length ? "All other components" : null, rest]]}))
}
```

```{ojs}
//| output: false
// fiscal years as buttons (client, 11/3: a dropdown hides an important filter). Shown at the top of the page, next to the question.
// Click a year, then another: that is the range. Click the same year twice for a single year.
viewof years = {
  const ok = y => y >= FY_FIRST && y <= FY_LAST
  const u = [+URLQ.get("from"), +URLQ.get("to")]
  const presets = [["All years", FY_FIRST, FY_LAST], ["Last 10", FY_LAST - 9, FY_LAST], ["Last 5", FY_LAST - 4, FY_LAST], [`FY${FY_LAST}`, FY_LAST, FY_LAST]]
  const pbtns = presets.map(([label, a, b]) => html`<button type="button" class="tl-p" data-a="${a}" data-b="${b}">${label}</button>`)
  const cells = d3.range(FY_FIRST, FY_LAST + 1).map(y => html`<button type="button" class="tl-y" data-y="${y}" title="FY${y}">${String(y).slice(2)}</button>`)
  const label = html`<span class="tl-label"></span>`
  const wrap = html`<div class="tl"><div class="tl-top">${pbtns}${label}</div><div class="tl-years">${cells}</div></div>`
  wrap.value = ok(u[0]) && ok(u[1]) ? [Math.min(...u), Math.max(...u)] : [FY_FIRST, FY_LAST]
  let anchor = null  // first click of a range
  const draw = () => {
    const [a, b] = wrap.value
    for (const c of cells) {
      const y = +c.dataset.y
      c.classList.toggle("on", anchor === null && y >= a && y <= b)
      c.classList.toggle("anchor", y === anchor)
      c.setAttribute("aria-pressed", y >= a && y <= b)
    }
    for (const p of pbtns) p.classList.toggle("on", anchor === null && +p.dataset.a === a && +p.dataset.b === b)
    label.textContent = anchor !== null ? `From FY${anchor}: now click the last year` : a === b ? `FY${a}` : `FY${a}–FY${b}`
  }
  const set = (a, b) => { wrap.value = [Math.min(a, b), Math.max(a, b)]; draw(); wrap.dispatchEvent(new Event("input", {bubbles: true})) }
  for (const p of pbtns) p.onclick = () => { anchor = null; set(+p.dataset.a, +p.dataset.b) }
  for (const c of cells) c.onclick = () => {
    const y = +c.dataset.y
    if (anchor === null) { anchor = y; draw(); return }
    const a = anchor
    anchor = null
    set(a, y)
  }
  draw()
  return wrap
}
```

```{ojs}
viewof compareWith = {
  // choosing adds to the comparison (no extra button): an agency adds the whole agency; then picking one of its
  // components replaces that whole-agency entry, and further components are added; up to 5; x removes one
  const agencySel = Object.assign(document.createElement("select"), {className: "form-select form-select-sm cmp-agency"})
  fillSelect(agencySel, [[null, [""]], ...AGENCY_GROUPS], a => a || "Choose an agency…")
  const compSel = html`<select class="form-select form-select-sm cmp-comp" disabled><option value="">Whole agency (all components)</option></select>`
  const chips = html`<div class="chips"></div>`
  const hint = html`<div class="side-note">Choosing adds it to the comparison; × removes it.</div>`
  const wrap = html`<div class="cmp"><div class="cmp-label">Compare with (up to 5)</div>${agencySel}${compSel}${hint}${chips}</div>`
  wrap.value = (URLQ.get("with") || "").split("~").filter(k => ENT.has(k)).slice(0, 5)
  let pending = null  // the entry the two lists currently point at
  const changed = () => wrap.dispatchEvent(new Event("input", {bubbles: true}))
  const draw = () => {
    chips.replaceChildren(...wrap.value.map(k => {
      const x = html`<button type="button" title="Remove">×</button>`
      x.onclick = () => { wrap.value = wrap.value.filter(v => v !== k); if (pending === k) pending = null; draw(); changed() }
      const twin = wrap.value.some(v => v !== k && ENT.get(v).short === ENT.get(k).short)  // same name at two agencies
      return html`<span class="chip">${twin ? ENT.get(k).label : ENT.get(k).short}${x}</span>`
    }))
    hint.textContent = wrap.value.length >= 5 ? "Up to 5: remove one (×) to add another." : "Choosing adds it to the comparison; × removes it."
  }
  const put = (key, replace) => {
    if (!ENT.has(key)) return
    let v = wrap.value.filter(k => k !== key)
    if (replace && v.includes(replace)) v = v.map(k => k === replace ? key : k)
    else if (v.length < 5) v = [...v, key]
    else return draw()
    wrap.value = [...new Set(v)]; pending = key; draw(); changed()
  }
  agencySel.addEventListener("change", () => {
    const a = agencySel.value
    const comps = ENTITIES.filter(e => e.key.startsWith(`C|${a}|`)).sort((x, y) => d3.ascending(x.short, y.short))
    compSel.replaceChildren(html`<option value="">${comps.length ? "Whole agency (all components)" : "No separate components"}</option>`,
      ...comps.map(e => html`<option value="${e.key}">${e.short}</option>`))
    compSel.disabled = !a || !comps.length
    if (a) put(`A|${a}`, null)
  })
  compSel.addEventListener("change", () => {
    const a = agencySel.value, key = compSel.value || `A|${a}`
    // the first component chosen replaces the whole agency that choosing the agency added
    put(key, pending === `A|${a}` && compSel.value ? pending : null)
  })
  draw()
  return wrap
}
```

```{ojs}
viewof scope = {
  // which agencies are added up in the government total: every agency that reported that year (the set grows over the
  // years, so part of the growth is new reporters), or the same agencies every year
  const keep = recall("scope", v => v === ALL_AG || v === COHORT, URLQ.get("scope") === "same" ? COHORT : ALL_AG)  // keep the choice when the input is rebuilt
  if (agency !== TOTAL) return hidden(keep)
  const radio = memo("scope", Inputs.radio([ALL_AG, COHORT], {label: "Agencies added up in the total", value: keep}))
  // the note goes inside the input itself, so the input keeps its value
  radio.append(html`<div class="side-note">The second keeps the same agencies every year, so growth is not just more agencies starting to report.</div>`)
  return radio
}
```

```{ojs}
//| output: false
yearX = Object({tickFormat: String, label: "Fiscal year"})
// bar charts: label every other year so the labels do not run together
yearBand = Object({tickFormat: d => d % 2 === 0 ? String(d) : "", label: "Fiscal year"})
// chart size from the window (cards report 0 size while a tab is hidden)
MAIN = width > 0 ? Math.max(560, window.innerWidth - 360) : 560  // depends on width, so it updates on resize
PAIR = Math.floor((MAIN - 70) / 2)
CH = Math.max(240, Math.min(560, window.innerHeight - 400))
TH = Math.max(260, window.innerHeight - 310)
lo = Math.min(fyFrom, fyTo)
hi = Math.max(fyFrom, fyTo)
cohortOnly = agency === TOTAL && scope === COHORT
// components of the chosen agency in the chosen years (key -> code and latest name), alphabetical
compChoices = agency === TOTAL ? [] : d3.groups(ROWS.filter(r => r.level === "component" && r.Agency === agency && r.FY >= lo && r.FY <= hi), r => r.Key)
  .map(([key, rs]) => { const last = d3.greatest(rs, r => r.FY); return {key, code: last.Component, name: last.Name} })
  .sort((a, b) => d3.ascending(a.name, b.name))
compName = k => { const x = compChoices.find(x => x.key === k); return x ? `${x.name} (${x.code})` : k }
// the selection: government total (agency rows), one agency's total, or one component
inSel = d => agency === TOTAL ? d.level === "agency" && (!cohortOnly || d.cohort)
  : comp === ALL ? d.level === "agency" && d.Agency === agency
  : d.level === "component" && d.Agency === agency && d.Key === comp
pick = rows => rows.filter(d => d.FY >= lo && d.FY <= hi && inSel(d))
// tables, last year chosen: every agency, or the chosen agency's total and its components
yearRows = rows => rows.filter(d => d.FY === hi && (agency === TOTAL ? d.level === "agency" && (!cohortOnly || d.cohort) : d.Agency === agency))
NAME_COL = agency === TOTAL ? "Agency" : "Component"
rowName = d => agency === TOTAL ? d.Agency : d.level === "agency" ? "(Agency total)" : `${d.Name} (${d.Component})`
who = agency === TOTAL ? (cohortOnly ? `${N_COHORT} agencies (all ${N_YEARS} years)` : "All reporting agencies")
  : comp === ALL ? `${agency}, all components` : `${agency} › ${compName(comp)}`
byYear = rows => rows.slice().sort((a, b) => a.FY - b.FY)
// years in which the selection has a report at all (shown when it does not cover the chosen years)
coverNote = (() => {
  if (agency === TOTAL) return ""
  const yrs = [...new Set(ROWS.filter(d => inSel(d)).map(d => d.FY))].sort((a, b) => a - b)
  if (!yrs.length) return ` · no reports in ${SPAN}`
  const inRange = yrs.filter(y => y >= lo && y <= hi)
  if (inRange.length === hi - lo + 1) return ""
  return yrs.length === yrs[yrs.length - 1] - yrs[0] + 1 ? ` · reports for FY${yrs[0]}–FY${yrs[yrs.length - 1]} only` : ` · reports for ${yrs.length} of the ${N_YEARS} years only`
})()
selName = agency === TOTAL ? (cohortOnly ? `${N_COHORT} agencies (total)` : "All agencies (total)") : comp === ALL ? agency : compName(comp)
entityRows = key => {
  const [lv, a, c] = key.split("|")
  return ROWS.filter(d => d.FY >= lo && d.FY <= hi && d.Agency === a && (lv === "A" ? d.level === "agency" : d.level === "component" && d.Key === c))
}
// an agency total already holds its components: say which one is on screen, and warn when a comparison overlaps (Anna, 11/3)
levelNote = agency === TOTAL ? "each agency counted once"
  : comp !== ALL ? "component: already inside the agency total"
  : compChoices.length ? "agency total: already includes its components" : "agency total"
overlapNote = (() => {
  const picked = [...(agency === TOTAL ? [] : [comp === ALL ? `A|${agency}` : `C|${agency}|${comp}`]), ...compareWith]
  const inside = picked.filter(k => k.startsWith("C|") && picked.includes(`A|${k.split("|")[1]}`))
  const code = k => (ENT.get(k).short.match(/\(([^)]+)\)$/) || [])[1] || ENT.get(k).short
  if (inside.length) return `${inside.map(code).join(", ")} ${inside.length > 1 ? "are" : "is"} already inside the agency total shown here: do not add them together.`
  if (agency === TOTAL && compareWith.length) return "Everything compared here is already inside the government total: do not add them together."
  return ""
})()
// what to look for in each step: how to read it, not what to conclude
function look(q) {
  if (lawsOn) return lawGuide()
  if (compareWith.length) return "Side by side. Agencies differ in size and in the kinds of records they hold, so a gap is a place to start asking questions, not a verdict."
  if (q === 1) {
    const rows = Q1.filter(d => d.level === "agency" && d.FY === hi && d.received != null && (!cohortOnly || d.cohort))
    const top = d3.greatest(rows, d => d.received), sum = d3.sum(rows, d => d.received)
    return `Compare received with processed: when processed stays below received, open requests build up.${agency === TOTAL && top && sum ? ` ${top.Agency} received ${pct(top.received / sum)} of all requests in FY${hi}, so the total mostly follows it.` : ""}`
  }
  if (q === 2) return "Read the three tracks separately. The basic time limit is 20 working days. Agencies sort requests into simple and complex themselves, so the same label can mean different things at different agencies."
  if (q === 3) return "All four measures start at 100, so their movement can be compared. Moving together does not show that one causes the other. Cost is not adjusted for inflation."
  if (q === 4) return "A full grant is only one way a request ends: others end with no records, withdrawn or referred. Exemptions count times applied, and one request can use several."
  if (q === 5) return "An appeal asks an agency to review its first decision. The rate depends on what it is divided by: appeals closed for other reasons, such as withdrawn, count only in the larger base."
  if (q === 6) return "Compare how fast the backlog grows with how fast requests grow. The backlog is a year-end count, so years cannot be added up."
  if (q === 7) return `${xtype === "04" ? "Days in this table are calendar days. " : ""}The right chart shows how many ${agency === TOTAL ? "agencies" : "components"} report this measure each year, so you can see where the data is thin.`
  return ""
}
// the view in the page address, so it can be shared
syncUrl = () => {
  const p = new URLSearchParams()
  if (qi) p.set("q", qi)
  if (agency !== TOTAL) p.set("agency", agency)
  if (agency !== TOTAL && comp !== ALL) p.set("comp", comp)
  if (lo !== FY_FIRST || hi !== FY_LAST) { p.set("from", lo); p.set("to", hi) }
  if (compareWith.length) p.set("with", compareWith.join("~"))
  if (cohortOnly) p.set("scope", "same")
  if (qi === 5 && base5 === "All processed appeals") p.set("base", "all")
  if (qi === 7) p.set("m", xcol)
  if (lawsOn) p.set("sub", "laws")
  const s = p.toString()
  history.replaceState(null, "", s ? `?${s}` : location.pathname)
}
function linkButton() {
  const b = html`<button type="button" class="stepbtn">Copy link to this view</button>`
  b.onclick = async () => {
    try { await navigator.clipboard.writeText(location.href); b.textContent = "Link copied" }
    catch (e) { b.textContent = "Copy it from the address bar" }
    setTimeout(() => { b.textContent = "Copy link to this view" }, 1800)
  }
  return b
}
function stepNav(q) {
  const i = STORY.indexOf(q)
  if (i < 0) return ""
  const go = (id, text) => { const b = html`<button type="button" class="stepbtn">${text}</button>`; b.onclick = () => openStep(id); return b }
  return html`<span class="stepnav">${i > 0 ? go(STORY[i - 1], "← Back") : go(0, "← Overview")}${i < STORY.length - 1
    ? go(STORY[i + 1], `Next: ${QUESTIONS[STORY[i + 1] - 1].short} →`) : go(7, "Explore all data →")}</span>`
}
```
